solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Type 'A secret I foolishly try to hide'

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within, so one piece goes inside the other
done foolishly, the letters of this phrase are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly attempts to conceal a secret, labelled as a type of behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' makes CATERISE; 'to hide' says the try is concealed within it. 'Type' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To type something is to classify it, assigning it to a class or group.

clue.text: Just goes to show which way the wind blows, mate

definitions.text: Just goes to show which way the wind blows
definitions.meaning: a weathercock or weathervane indicates wind direction; the bird on top gives the short name
an informal British form of address to a friend

explanation.surface: A proverbial remark to a friend about how things are trending.
explanation.definitionFit: A weathercock is often called simply a cock, and cock is old British slang for a pal.

clue.text: Until dream shatters, going through daily grind

indicators.note: one piece passes through the middle of the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: till is a short form of until

indicators.note: a dream that shatters breaks into pieces, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A shattered dream drives someone on through the monotony of daily work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shatters' gives READM, and 'going through' sets it within the word for until.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a figurative term for wearisome routine work, the same as a daily grind.

clue.text: To make money is disgusting

definitions.meaning: to earn a sum before deductions

explanation.surface: A moralist's view that profit-making is distasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means earning a total before tax; as an adjective it means revolting.

clue.text: Get going again and others pitch in

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: the rest means the others
pitch is a black tarry substance, so tar

explanation.surface: A team resuming play once the others join in on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field but is the sticky black stuff, TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin once more after stopping, a direct synonym.

clue.text: 'When tourists abound,' they add

definitions.meaning: the holiday season, summer months, plural
people who sum figures, i.e. add them up

explanation.surface: A quoted remark about peak season, with someone adding their comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Summers are the warm seasons crowded with holidaymakers; summers are also people who total numbers.

clue.text: Cheat one into providing money

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to con is to swindle or cheat
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Tricking someone into handing over cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin is metal currency, a form of money in general.

clue.text: Not once has one slid foot inside

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another
letters that have slid have shifted position, so they are rearranged

parts.note: ft is the standard abbreviation for foot as a unit of length

explanation.surface: Someone has slipped more than once, a foot sliding indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slid' gives OEN, and 'inside' puts the abbreviation for foot within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done frequently happens many times rather than a single time.

clue.text: Not a novice? It's not running

definitions.meaning: whimsically, someone who is no beginner
a horse or idea that has no chance, or that won't take part

explanation.surface: Questioning someone's experience, then noting a machine has stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-starter is a horse withdrawn from a race, hence anything that has no prospect of success.

clue.text: Belief in decorating? A semi conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes the form of something, so the letters are rearranged
semi means half, so only the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone's philosophy of home improvement: converting a semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A semi' takes half of DECORATING, DECOR, and 'conversion' rearranges it. A semi is also a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or set of principles someone holds.

clue.text: A fool but no trouble: not unruly

parts.note: something that is no trouble is simple or easy

indicators.note: unruly letters are disorderly, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A description of someone foolish yet easy to manage, not unruly at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish or gullible person, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Having muffed goal, run with depleted energy

indicators.note: to muff is to bungle, so the letters are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer, having missed the goal, runs on with tired legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muffed' rearranges GOAL and RUN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a state of tiredness or listlessness, a lack of vigour.

clue.text: Sickness, when waters abate, will go round

indicators.note: one piece encircles the other

parts.note: to abate is to die down, as wind does, so die
the waters of the world are the seas

explanation.surface: A warning that illness will spread once floodwaters recede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abate' pairs with 'waters' in the surface but is a separate piece, meaning to die down as wind does; 'go round' wraps it about the waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Disease is an illness or disorder of the body, the same as sickness.

clue.text: Tennis court not equipped for the players' performance?

definitions.meaning: a court lacking its net has ..., read as one word
a piece for nine musicians to play

explanation.surface: A tennis court missing its equipment, as a question about the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine instruments or the group of nine who perform it.

clue.text: Strong defence to tie the game

parts.note: a tied match is a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A solid defensive display earning a tied result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong defence' sounds like football, but it is a castle's raising bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge can be raised to protect a castle entrance, part of its fortifications.

clue.text: Clothing I am untidily ramming into breach

indicators.note: one piece is forced into the middle of the other

parts.note: a rent is a tear or breach

indicators.note: arranged untidily, the letters are put in a messy new order

explanation.surface: Someone stuffing clothes carelessly into a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidily' gives AIM, which 'ramming into' forces into the word for breach.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: 'Dispatch' I spelt otherwise; with an E

indicators.note: spelt otherwise means written in a different order

parts.note: the letter E as given

explanation.surface: A writer admits spelling a word differently, adding an E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges I SPELT into EPISTL, then E goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, and a dispatch is a message sent to someone.

clue.text: Tell nobody — say 'Keep things dark'

parts.note: sh is the call for hush, telling someone to keep quiet
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a secret and stay in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To shutter windows is to close their screens and so block out the light.

clue.text: Score and feel low

parts.note: to touch is to feel
feeling low is feeling down

explanation.surface: A footballer scores and then feels depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby or American football a touchdown is a scoring play.

clue.text: Fools are wise, contriving to take everybody in

indicators.note: to take something in is to enclose it
with 'to take', signals that one piece is held within the other
contriving means devising, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Clever people scheming to deceive the whole world are fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contriving' gives WIES, and 'to take ... in' holds everybody within it; take in also means deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallies is British slang for silly or inept people, so fools.

clue.text: Has he put paid to his days of wandering?

definitions.text: Has he put paid to his days of wandering?

parts.words: Has he put paid to his days of wandering?
parts.note: a person who stops roaming and puts down roots, also one who pays up a bill

explanation.walkthrough: 'put paid' hints at settling an account, while ending a wandering life is settling down.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is someone who makes a permanent home somewhere, ending a nomadic life.

clue.text: Transferring our bag, about to go on a spree

indicators.note: one piece goes about, i.e. around, the other

parts.note: a case is a bag for carrying things

indicators.note: transferring moves the letters around, so they change order

explanation.surface: Someone moves their luggage and heads off on a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transferring' turns OUR into ROU, and CASE goes 'about' it: CA-ROU-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily, as on a spree.

clue.text: Ticked off child when I'd got home

parts.note: the letters of I'd without the apostrophe
a den is an animal's home or a cosy room

explanation.surface: A child is told off for coming home late.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old past participle of chide, to scold or rebuke.

clue.text: Criticise star performing (band included)

indicators.note: one piece is included within the other
letters performing go through moves, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a ring or band is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A critic slates a star's show, with the band in it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns STAR into RAST, and O goes inside after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them harshly, informal usage.

clue.text: Hears he left on, starting a fire

indicators.note: he left means those two letters depart from the word

parts.note: the letters of he as written

explanation.surface: Someone hears a person left something switched on, which caused a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction but means departed: HE leaves HEARS, giving ARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Capturing power I'm hurt badly but succeed

indicators.note: one piece holds another within it
letters arranged badly are set in a disordered way

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Despite injury, someone wins the title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IMHURT as TRIUMH, and 'Capturing' takes P inside it before the H.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph is to win or be victorious, so to succeed.

clue.text: Gracious, it's fuzzy inside. Hard to see

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: 'Gracious!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: a fuzzy arrangement is blurred, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that their head feels fuzzy and they can't see well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' and 'My' are both exclamations of surprise; 'fuzzy' scrambles it's, set 'inside' the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Misty conditions blur vision, so things are obscured and difficult to make out.

clue.text: Observe, when you turn to look

indicators.note: turning the word round means reading it backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Watching what happens as you turn to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or holiday is to observe it, i.e. honour or comply with it.

clue.text: Banished for a while, died out

indicators.note: one piece is outside the other

parts.note: the word died as written
a spell is a period of time, a while

explanation.surface: Something banished for a time eventually faded away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'died out' reads as faded away, but 'out' is the container signal: the period of time sits within the word died.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or dismiss, so dispelled fits banished.

clue.text: Jewel that, misguidedly, the nest egg went into

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other
letters placed misguidedly are put in the wrong order

parts.note: an egg is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone's savings unwisely went into buying a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguidedly' gives STNE, and the egg shape 'went into' it; 'nest egg' is a red herring for savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is a gem, a precious jewel in a setting.

clue.text: Be paid, reportedly, as a high flier

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or spoken, so the word is matched by sound

parts.note: to earn is to be paid for work

explanation.surface: A high-flying executive's salary, described by hearsay.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a bird soaring at height.

clue.text: With spirit, say angrily 'You can eat it'

parts.note: brandy is a distilled spirit
to snap is to speak sharply

explanation.surface: A drunk person snapping 'you can eat it' at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger biscuit, a British treat.
